title: Spherical Flows for Sampling Categorical Data
claim: Our noise path with predictor-corrector sampling achieves a better quality-diversity tradeoff than alternatives, beating baselines at matched entropy.
layout: 1 panel, log-scale line plot, vertical dashed and horizontal dotted reference lines
description: A single line plot of generation perplexity (log y-axis, 15 to 300) against sample entropy in nats (x-axis, about 3.95 to 4.4). Four curves with markers: solid blue vMF, dashed magenta vMF+SC with open circles, orange VP, and purple VP+SC with open circles. The magenta curve sits lowest, rising from about 19 PPL at low entropy to about 80 near the data entropy. The blue curve lies above it. The orange and purple curves cluster in a short segment at high entropy. A vertical dashed black line marks H_data near 4.34. A horizontal dotted gray line marks the AR baseline at 66.7 PPL, labeled 'no H'. Gray diamonds mark the reference methods FLM, LangFlow and DFM Diag. The legend is at upper left. The eye goes first to the magenta curve at the bottom.
caption: LM1B gen. PPL against entropy at NFE = 128, sweeping ε; every curve is predictor-corrector. References that report an entropy are placed at it, AR is drawn as a horizontal line. Data entropy Hdata as a vertical dashed line. Configuration in Appendix D.1.3.
abstract: We study the problem of learning generative models for discrete sequences in a continuous embedding space. Whereas prior approaches typically operate in Euclidean space or on the probability simplex, we instead work on the sphere $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. There the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution induces a natural noise process and admits a closed-form conditional score. The conditional velocity is in general intractable. Exploiting the radial symmetry of the vMF density we reduce the continuity equation on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ to a scalar ODE in the cosine similarity, whose unique bounded solution determines the velocity. The marginal velocity and marginal score on $(\mathbb S^{d-1})^L$ both decompose into posterior-weighted tangent sums that differ only by per-token scalar weights. This gives access to both ODE and predictor-corrector (PC) sampling. The posterior is the only learned object, trained by a cross-entropy loss. Experiments compare the vMF path against geodesic and Euclidean alternatives. The vMF path especially in combination with PC sampling significantly improves results on Sudoku, language modeling, and mathematical reasoning.
